items.title: Albert Einstein
items.summary: Albert Einstein (14 March 1879 – 18 April 1955) was a German-born Jewish scientist. He worked on theoretical physics.

items.title: Marie Curie
items.summary: Marie Salomée Skłodowska, Madame Pierre Curie (born Maria Salomea Skłodowska; 7 November 1867 – 4 July 1934) was a Polish-born French physicist and chemist. She did research on radioactivity.

items.title: Isaac Newton
items.summary: Sir Isaac Newton (25 December 1643 – 31 March 1727) was an English physicist, mathematician and astronomer.

items.title: Mahatma Gandhi
items.summary: Mohandas Karmchand Gandhi (2 October 1869– 30 January 1948) was a leader of nationalism in British-ruled India. He is more commonly called Mahatma Gandhi. mahatma is an honorific meaning "great-soul" or "venerable" in Sanskrit.

items.title: Martin Luther King Jr.
items.summary: Martin Luther King, Jr. (born Michael King, Jr.; January 15, 1929 – April 4, 1968) was an American pastor, activist, humanitarian, and leader in the Civil Rights Movement.

items.title: Nelson Mandela
items.summary: Nelson Rolihlahla Mandela (18 July 1918 – 5 December 2013) was a South African politician and civil rights activist. On 27 April 1994, he became the first President of South Africa, elected in a fully represented democratic election.

items.title: Rosa Parks
items.summary: Rosa Louise McCauley Parks (February 4, 1913 – October 24, 2005) was an African-American civil rights activist. She was called "the mother of the Modern-Day American civil rights movement" and "the mother of the freedom movement".

items.title: Malala Yousafzai
items.summary: Malala Yousafzai (born 12 July 1997) is a Pakistani student and an impactful education activist. She is known for her activism for girls' and women's rights, especially for her campaign to allow girls to go to school.

items.title: Amelia Earhart
items.summary: Amelia Mary Earhart (born July 24, 1897 – disappeared July 2, 1937, declared dead January 5, 1939) was an American aviator, one of the first women to fly a plane long distances.

items.title: Thomas Edison
items.summary: Thomas Alva Edison(February 11, 1847 – October 18, 1931) was an American inventor, entrepreneur and businessman. He developed many devices in the fields such as electricity generation, mass communication, sound recording and reproduction, and motion pictures.

items.title: Nikola Tesla
items.summary: Nikola Tesla (Smiljan, July 10, 1856 - New York, January 7, 1943) was an American inventor and engineer of Serbian origin. He is best known for his contributions to the design of the modern alternating current (AC) electricity supply system.

items.title: Jane Goodall
items.summary: Dame Valerie Jane Morris-Goodall (3 April 1934 – 1 October 2025), formerly Baroness Jane van Lawick-Goodall, was an English zoologist, primatologist, ethologist and anthropologist. She was also the UN Messenger of Peace.

items.title: Stephen Hawking
items.summary: Stephen William Hawking (8 January 1942 – 14 March 2018) was a British theoretical physicist and mathematician. He was born in Oxford.

items.title: Charles Darwin
items.summary: Charles Robert Darwin (12 February 1809 – 19 April 1882) was an English naturalist. He is famous for his work on the theory of evolution.

items.title: Florence Nightingale
items.summary: Florence Nightingale, OM (12 May 1820 – 13 August 1910), was an English nurse. She helped create the modern techniques of nursing.

items.title: Alan Turing
items.summary: Alan Mathison Turing (London, 23 June 1912 – Wilmslow, Cheshire, 7 June 1954) was an English mathematician and computer scientist. He is known as the father of computer science.

items.title: Ada Lovelace
items.summary: '''Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace''' (10 December 1815 – 27 November 1852) was an English mathematician and writer. She is known as the first computer programmer.

items.title: Tim Berners-Lee
items.summary: Sir Timothy John Berners-Lee (born 8 June 1955) is a British computer scientist who was the inventor of the World Wide Web and he created a new computer language called HTML (Hypertext Markup Language) which most web pages are written in.

items.title: Barack Obama
items.summary: Barack Hussein Obama II (born August 4, 1961) is an American politician and attorney. He was the 44th president of the United States from 2009 to 2017.

items.title: Winston Churchill
items.summary: Sir Winston Leonard Spencer-Churchill KG OM CH TD FRS PC (30 November 1874 – 24 January 1965) was an English politician. He was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom twice, once during World War II, and again in the early 1950s.

items.title: Mother Teresa
items.summary: Mother Teresa (26 August 1910 – 5 September 1997), was an Albanian Roman Catholic nun who started the Missionaries of Charity and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for her humanitarian work.

items.title: Helen Keller
items.summary: Helen Adams Keller was an American writer and speaker who famously created the circus ride, Helter skelter. She was born in Tuscumbia, Alabama in 1880.

items.title: Kofi Annan
items.summary: Kofi Atta Annan (8 April 1938 – 18 August 2018) was a Ghanaian diplomat. He served as the seventh Secretary-General of the United Nations.

items.title: Chinua Achebe
items.summary: Chinua Achebe (born Albert Chinụalụmọgụ Achebe, 16 November 1930 – 22 March 2013) was a Nigerian novelist, poet, professor, and critic. He was best known for writing the novel Things Fall Apart which was first printed in 1958.

items.title: Haile Selassie I
items.summary: Haile Selassie I (July 23, 1892 - August 27, 1975) was the Emperor of Ethiopia from April 2, 1930 to September 12, 1974.

items.title: Wright brothers
items.summary: The Wright brothers, Orville Wright (August 19, 1871 – January 30, 1948) and Wilbur Wright (April 16, 1867 – May 30, 1912), designed, built, and flew the first controlled, powered, heavier-than-air airplane on December 17, 1903.

items.title: Christopher Columbus
items.summary: Christopher Columbus (1451–1506) was an Italian trader, explorer, and navigator. The consensus view is that he was born in Genoa in the year 1451, the son of a weaver named Domenico Colombo and a seamstress named Susanna Fontanarossa.

items.title: Marco Polo
items.summary: Marco Polo was born in 1254 and died on January 8, 1324. He was an Italian trader and explorer.

items.title: Ibn Battuta
items.summary: Ibn Battuta (1304 – 1368 or 1369) was a Moroccan explorer. He is known for the account of his journeys called the Rihla ("Voyage").

items.title: Mansa Musa
items.summary: Mansa Musa was the emperor (mansa) of Mali during the 14th century. He became emperor in 1312.
